review.summary:
changes_needed
Fan-in can count duplicates or unrelated hypotheses toward a feed ticket.
Escalated conflicts remain eligible for ticket creation.
The handoff sketch discards evidence and does not enforce its turn cap.
Validation: 25 tests passed; link checker reports bad 0.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: code sketches do what the text says
findings.title: Count distinct sites confirming the feed hypothesis toward quorum
findings.claim: The purported 3-of-5 feed quorum counts every confirmed W2 finding, regardless of hypothesis or duplicate site. It can therefore authorize a fleet feed ticket without three sites confirming a feed outage.
findings.evidence: Executing the fan-in block with diagnostic stubs returned fleet_ticket=True for three duplicate feed findings from PVA-01. It also returned True for three meter findings from different W2 sites, with no feed findings.
findings.proposed_change: Filter for the feed hypothesis and the five eligible W2 sites, then count distinct site identities with valid confirmations. Verify that duplicates and unrelated hypotheses cannot satisfy quorum.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: code sketches do what the text says
findings.title: Remove unresolved conflicting votes before authorizing tickets
findings.claim: Escalating a contradictory group does not remove its findings from the later quorum. The code can both escalate a site's conflicting evidence and count that site's confirmation toward a ticket, unlike the diagram's separate conflict and quorum paths.
findings.evidence: Running the block with confirmed feed findings for three sites and a rejected feed finding for one of those same sites produced one escalation and fleet_ticket=True. Only two sites had unconflicted confirmations.
findings.proposed_change: Record unresolved conflicting groups and exclude their votes before evaluating quorum. Distinguish same-site contradictions from disagreement between independently checked sites. Verify that two valid confirmations plus one conflicted site cannot satisfy a three-site quorum.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: code sketches do what the text says
findings.title: Deliver the handoff payload to the receiving agent
findings.claim: The sketch parses the evidence into local variable p but never delivers or saves it. It also never appends the assistant response or collected tool results to st.messages. The receiving agent consequently cannot see the evidence the lesson requires.
findings.evidence: The only use of p is its assignment. The next model call reads history_for(st.active, st.messages), while results is a separate list. Executing the unchanged block with diagnostic stubs left st.messages empty and passed empty histories to every receiving-agent call.
findings.proposed_change: Persist the validated payload in receiver-visible state, append the response and matched tool results to the transcript, and construct the receiving history from that saved state. Check that typed evidence survives both remove-tools filtering and checkpoint resume.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: stopping conditions and guards
findings.title: Make the handoff loop advance and enforce its limits
findings.claim: The loop never increments turn, handles completion, or checks st.handoffs. Neither its displayed turn cap nor the worked answer's handoff cap actually stops execution.
findings.evidence: With turn=0 and cap=1, the unchanged block reached four model calls before a diagnostic stub interrupted it; turn remained 0 and three handoffs had already occurred. A response without tool calls also reaches save(st) and loops again.
findings.proposed_change: Advance a checkpointed turn counter, handle normal completion, and reject a fourth handoff before changing the active agent. Verify termination for a final response, repeated handoffs, and exhaustion of the turn budget.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: partial-failure behavior in code sketches
findings.title: Preserve successful branches when a completed worker raises
findings.claim: A completed task may contain an exception. Calling t.result() without handling it aborts the whole merge, defeating the partial-with-flags policy described in the worked answer.
findings.evidence: Executing the block with one successful worker, one worker raising RuntimeError, and one late worker raised RuntimeError before producing a merge result. The successful finding was not returned, and the late task remained running.
findings.proposed_change: Collect outcomes per task, convert worker failures into typed untested/error entries, and cancel and await late tasks. Verify that a failed worker preserves healthy findings and leaves no pending workers.

findings.checklist_item: A. Accuracy: worked answers answer the exercise as configured
findings.title: Give specialists the return handoff used in the worked answer
findings.claim: Neither specialist has a handoff tool, so the worked answer's feed-specialist return to triage and resulting ping-pong cannot occur with the specified tool sets.
findings.evidence: Only triage receives transfer tools at lines 278–280. Line 310 nevertheless says the feed specialist 'hands back' before triage transfers to the site specialist. The lesson itself says control returns only through another handoff.
findings.proposed_change: Add transfer_to_triage to the relevant specialists and describe the permitted return paths, or revise the worked answer to match terminal specialists. Run the ambiguous PVA-04 case using exactly the documented tools.

findings.checklist_item: Plain language: code and its explanation must communicate the same contract
findings.title: Include concrete scope identities in the finding schema
findings.claim: The proposed schema records only whether a scope is a site or cluster. It cannot identify which site or cluster produced a finding, although later grouping, deduplication and quorum require those identities.
findings.evidence: The schema has scope: Literal['site', 'cluster'] and no scope_id, site or cluster field. The fan-in at lines 383–388 reads f.scope_id and f.cluster; the worked answer at line 437 sorts by site.
findings.proposed_change: Define a consistent contract with scope kind, concrete scope identity, site identity where applicable, and cluster membership. Use those fields throughout the examples and verify that findings for different sites remain distinguishable.
